anzsic_codes.name: Other Specialised Industrial Machinery and Equipment Wholesaling

merger_description:
Jaybro Group Pty Ltd (**Jaybro**) proposes to acquire 100% of the issued shares of Sewer Equipment Company Australia (the **Acquisition**).

Jaybro is an Australian company that specialises in the supply of infrastructure services, materials and consumables for civil and construction projects. Through its Jaybro and Cadia brands, Jaybro supplies a range of pipe and associated underground utility products used in civil construction, as well as civil consumables.

Jaybro is majority owned by Quadrant Private Equity No. 7A (of which the trustee entity is QPE No. 7A Pty Limited) (**Quadrant Fund 7**). Quadrant Fund 7 completed its acquisition of Jaybro from CPE Capital on 28 February 2022. Quadrant Fund 7 is a fund of QPE.

Sewer Equipment Company Australia is an Australian business that supplies equipment and software for the cleaning, testing, inspection and rehabilitation of pipes, sewers and drains. Sewer Equipment Company Australia is the trading name for the business held by Nordkapp Investments Pty Ltd and Mark Quealy Pty Ltd.

Sewer Equipment Company Australia’s product range includes CCTV inspection equipment and software, drain cleaning equipment, pipeline testing equipment, pipe rehabilitation equipment, operator and manhole tools, nozzles, customised vehicle builds, equipment servicing and repairs, and WinCan software support and training. Sewer Equipment Company Australia also provides training on how to use the equipment it sells.

Sewer Equipment Company Australia primarily supplies its products to service providers involved in liquid waste collection and maintenance services. Sewer Equipment Company Australia operates nationally, with an online store and office locations in Sydney (Chipping Norton), Brisbane (Ormeau) and Melbourne (Dandenong South).

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is a small horizontal overlap between Jaybro and
Sewer Equipment Company Australia in the supply of drain
and sewer-related inspection and maintenance equipment in
Australia
b. there are alternative suppliers of drain and sewer-related
inspection and maintenance equipment in Australia
c. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects resulting from exclusionary conduct post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
